name: kibi-mcp

tools.name: kb_query
tools.description: Read entities from the KB with exact filters, or ask typed fact questions. Use for lookup by id, type, tags or sourceFile, and for precise questions about modeled facts: predicate facts by name with named arguments (predicate + where), property facts of a subject (subjectKey + propertyKey), the domain view of a subject (factKind 'subject' + subjectKey: its definition, broader and narrower subjects, every current requirement about it and the claims and scenarios on it), or the catalog of facts of one kind (factKind; 'predicate_schema' lists the predicates you can ask about with their argument names and constants). Typed answers return matching fact rows plus factQuery: the schema used, distinct counts, values that do exist when nothing matched, warnings about the question and the next call to make. Read-only. Tags filter by metadata tags only, not entity IDs.

kb.description: Optional KB dependency name from .kb/dependencies.json to read, at its pinned commit, instead of this project's KB.

type.description: Optional entity type filter. Allowed: req, scenario, test, adr, flag, event, symbol, fact. Example: 'req'.

id.description: Optional exact entity ID. Example: 'REQ-cli-gc'. If omitted, returns matching entities by other filters.

tags.description: Optional tag filter. Matches entities that contain any provided tag. Example: ['security','billing'].

sourceFile.description: Optional source-file substring filter. Example: 'src/auth/login.ts'. Uses KB source linkage, not file-system scanning.

factKind.description: Typed fact filter: list facts of one kind; 'predicate_schema' returns the catalog of askable predicates.

predicate.description: Typed fact filter: predicate name to ask about; returns its stored facts with arguments, polarity and effect.

namespace.description: Optional predicate namespace when the same name exists in several. Default: any namespace.

where.description: Named argument values for predicate, using the names from its schema.

args.description: Positional argument values for a predicate with no schema; null matches any. Prefer where.

polarity.description: Optional polarity filter for predicate facts. Default: both.

scope.description: Optional: 'current_requirements' keeps only facts a current (not superseded or retired) requirement requires.

distinct.description: Optional argument name whose distinct values to count across the matching predicate facts.

subjectKey.description: Typed fact filter: dotted subject key whose property facts to list; combine with propertyKey or factKind 'subject'.

propertyKey.description: Optional property key under subjectKey, e.g. 'max_roles'. Returns operator, value and unit of each fact.

limit.description: Optional max rows to return after filtering. Default: 100 when omitted. Example: 25.

offset.description: Optional zero-based pagination offset. Default: 0. Example: 50 to skip first 50 rows.

includeBody.description: With id only: also return the entity's authored Markdown body. Default: false.

workspaceRoot.description: Optional absolute path of the workspace this call is about, such as your git worktree, when it is not the server's.

tools.name: kb_search
tools.description: Ask the KB a question or search it. Default intent-v1 ranking accepts questions, host-agent semantic facets and changed-code source locations, returns evidence, abstains below its confidence threshold and adds an answer layer: the current requirements that govern the topic with their statement and recorded reason (why), what must stay true (linked facts), the deciding ADRs and what verifies it (scenarios, tests). A weak answer may add queryAnalysis.hints from a search-hints plugin: requirements the question may mean, to re-ask with. Use before changing behavior, then kb_query for exact follow-up. No mutation side effects.

kb.description: Optional KB dependency name from .kb/dependencies.json to read, at its pinned commit, instead of this project's KB.

query.description: Free-text query for metadata and markdown body discovery. Example: 'OAuth login flow'.

type.description: Optional entity type filter to narrow discovery. Example: 'req'.

limit.description: Optional max rows after ranking. Default: 10; raise it or page with offset when the answer layer is not enough.

rankingMode.description: Optional ranking mode: intent-v1 (default, question-aware) or legacy (older lexical ranking).

answer.description: Intent-v1, first page: when true (default), include the answer layer of governing requirements and their evidence.

hints.description: Intent-v1, first page: when true (default), a weak answer adds hints from a kibi.search-hints.v1 plugin.

semanticFacets.description: Optional host-agent interpretations Kibi uses as deterministic aliases and facets; ranking never calls a model.

sourceLocations.description: Optional changed-code locations. Results are matched to source-linked symbols/entities and include source evidence.

minScore.description: Intent-v1 acceptance threshold between 0 and 1. Low-confidence queries abstain instead of returning misleading matches.

fields.description: Optional result detail: 'summary' (metadata, snippet) or 'full' (also bodies, graph paths, fact kb_query calls).

workspaceRoot.description: Optional absolute path of the workspace this call is about, such as your git worktree, when it is not the server's.

tools.name: kb_status
tools.description: Report current branch, KB snapshot, freshness metadata, schema status, and a typed kibi.migration-plan.v2 action graph. Call it first to orient on a branch or after a failed call; use kb_check for validation findings and kb_coverage for proof status. Read-only status inspection with no mutation side effects; damaged stores are diagnosed without starting the engine.

kb.description: Optional KB dependency name from .kb/dependencies.json to read, at its pinned commit, instead of this project's KB.

workspaceRoot.description: Optional absolute path of the workspace this call is about, such as your git worktree, when it is not the server's.

tools.name: kb_skills
tools.description: Read bundled Kibi agent skills (workflow guidance). action:list returns the catalog; action:load returns a skill's metadata, Markdown body, declared resources and content hash (start with id 'kibi-usage'); action:read returns one manifest-declared resource. Read-only; does not require Prolog.

action.description: list, load (needs id) or read (needs id and resource).

resource.description: Manifest-declared resource path to read. Example: 'resources/workflows.md'.

workspaceRoot.description: Optional absolute path of the workspace this call is about, such as your git worktree, when it is not the server's.

tools.name: kb_find_gaps
tools.description: List KB entities by the relationships they lack or have. Use for questions like which requirements lack scenarios or tests; all filters must match, and a relationship counts in either direction. Use kb_coverage instead for proof status and repair plans, and kb_check for rule violations. No mutation side effects.

kb.description: Optional KB dependency name from .kb/dependencies.json to read, at its pinned commit, instead of this project's KB.

type.description: Only report entities of this type. Omit for all types.

missingRelationships.description: Relationship types the entity must have none of, e.g. specified_by or verified_by.

presentRelationships.description: Relationship types the entity must have at least one of each, in either direction.

tags.description: Keep entities carrying any of these metadata tags.

sourceFile.description: Keep entities whose source path contains this substring.

limit.description: Maximum rows to return; count reports the full total.

workspaceRoot.description: Optional absolute path of the workspace this call is about, such as your git worktree, when it is not the server's.

tools.name: kb_coverage
tools.description: Generate curated structural coverage and conservative end-to-end requirement proof reports for requirements, symbols, or grouped types. Use it to ask which requirements are tested end to end, how strong each requirement's evidence is (evidenceLevel: proved, tested, asserted or unverified), and what blocks the rest; use kb_find_gaps for a plain list of missing links and kb_check for rule violations. Reports include the compatible repair plan plus typed kibi.migration-plan.v2 actions; semantic and E2E actions remain review/execution work. Paginated plans identify incomplete scope and no mutation occurs.

kb.description: Optional KB dependency name from .kb/dependencies.json to read, at its pinned commit, instead of this project's KB.

by.description: Report shape: req (proof status and repair plan), symbol (ownership coverage) or type (counts per type).

tags.description: Keep rows for entities carrying any of these metadata tags.

includePassing.description: Also return rows that are already tested or not applicable. By default only rows that still need repair are returned.

statuses.description: req mode: include only rows whose proofStatus is listed. The summary always covers the whole KB.

includeTransitive.description: Count symbol coverage reached transitively through linked entities, not only direct links.

limit.description: Maximum rows to return. When the repair plan reports scope.complete false, rerun with offset 0 and a larger limit.

includeMigrationPreview.description: Opt in to a deterministic, read-only kibi.legacy-migration-plan.v1 preview for ready semantic-inventory repair batches.

migrationLimit.description: Maximum requirement migration batches to preview. Defaults to one review batch.

migrationOffset.description: Zero-based offset into ready semantic-inventory batches.

migrationPredicateLimit.description: Maximum exact predicate-schema candidates retained per assertive proposition.

migrationPredicateMinScore.description: Minimum deterministic predicate-schema rank score retained in migration previews.

workspaceRoot.description: Optional absolute path of the workspace this call is about, such as your git worktree, when it is not the server's.

tools.name: kb_graph
tools.description: Run bounded graph traversal from one or more seed IDs across curated relationship types and return the nodes and edges reached. Use it to follow links from IDs you already have, such as a requirement to its scenarios and tests or a symbol to the requirements it implements; use kb_query to find entities by filter and kb_search to ask a question. Traversal stops at depth, maxNodes or maxEdges and then sets truncated. No mutation side effects.

kb.description: Optional KB dependency name from .kb/dependencies.json to read, at its pinned commit, instead of this project's KB.

seedIds.description: Entity IDs to start from, for example REQ-... or SCEN-.... Seeds are always returned as nodes.

relationships.description: Relationship types to follow, e.g. specified_by, verified_by or implements. Omit to follow every type.

direction.description: outgoing follows links from each node, incoming follows links pointing at it, both does either.

depth.description: Number of hops from the seeds.

entityTypes.description: Keep only nodes of these types and the edges between them; traversal still passes through other types.

maxNodes.description: Stop and set truncated once this many nodes are reached.

maxEdges.description: Stop and set truncated once this many edges are reached.

workspaceRoot.description: Optional absolute path of the workspace this call is about, such as your git worktree, when it is not the server's.

tools.name: kb_model
tools.description: Turn requirement prose into checkable structure without writing the KB. Use it for one requirement's prose; to plan a whole change request use kb_compile_intent. mode:analyze returns the semantic advisor receipt: the clause ledger, what is grounded, what is ambiguous and suggested modeling (pass clauses for compound prose and optional typed kibi.logic.v1 interpretations). mode:requirement converts one claim (subjectKey, propertyKey, operator, value, or typed logic) into a strict-lane write set and applyPlan. mode:predicates ranks ontology predicate schemas and returns an applicable predicate-fact plan only for reviewed bindings, otherwise an ontology-gap observation. With requirementId, mode:predicates also returns a hash-bound plan (fact write plus requires_predicate link) for kb_apply_plan, whose contradictionAnalysis is the what-if over the current KB; other returned plans apply with kb_upsert, and kb_upsert dryRun with plannedFacts previews a requirement before its facts exist.

mode.description: analyze (advisor receipt), requirement (strict claim write set) or predicates (ontology predicate plan).

text.description: Required prose requirement text to model. Example: 'Customer data must be retained for 7 years.'

clauses.description: Optional complete list of atomic clauses; each must be a verbatim fragment of text.

interpretations.description: Optional typed kibi.logic.v1 interpretations from the host model; raw Prolog is not accepted.

type.description: Entity type context for analysis; only requirements receive deterministic modeling suggestions.

id.description: Optional requirement ID used for deterministic draft relationship guidance.

title.description: Optional requirement title for draft apply plans.

source.description: Optional primary source path used for stable IDs and text refs.

status.description: Optional requirement status for draft suggestions.

requirementId.description: Optional requirement ID the strict write set updates instead of minting a REQ-AUTO id.

subjectHint.description: Optional canonical subject key to use as the first predicate argument. Example: 'editor.annotation'.

maxCandidates.description: Maximum ranked predicate candidates to return. Default: 5.

minScore.description: Minimum candidate score. Higher values make ontology-gap fallback more likely. Default: 0.35.

includeExistingSchemas.description: Whether to include the KB's predicate_schema facts beside the built-in predicate catalog. Default: true.

schemaId.description: Optional exact reviewed predicate schema ID to use instead of rank order; fails closed if unavailable.

argumentBindings.description: Optional exact predicate argument values keyed by argument name; required when binding_status is incomplete.

polarityHint.description: Optional reviewed polarity override when surface negation does not mean predicate denial.

existingLogicClaims.description: Existing requirement logic_claims values; the update merges the new claim key into them.

sourceFiles.description: Optional related source files. The first value is used as the source fallback when source is omitted.

confidence.description: Confidence of the extracted claim: >= 0.70 yields strict-lane output, lower yields observation-only output.

subjectKey.description: Optional extracted semantic claim subjectKey. Example: 'Customer.Data'.

propertyKey.description: Optional extracted semantic claim propertyKey. Example: 'Retention Years'.

operator.description: Optional claim operator, e.g. eq, gt, lt; sets take eq, includes, subset_of or excludes; matches takes a regex.

value.description: Optional claim value: string, number, boolean, or a list of strings for a set claim.

provenance.description: Optional extracted text reference; falls back to source. Example: '.kb/requirements/customer-retention.md#L1'.

claimKey.description: Optional advisor-issued claim key for the exact proposition represented by logic.

claimText.description: Optional exact proposition text represented by logic; defaults to text.

logic.description: Optional typed kibi.logic.v1 IR. Kibi validates and canonicalizes it into a rule fact; raw Prolog is rejected.

workspaceRoot.description: Optional absolute path of the workspace this call is about, such as your git worktree, when it is not the server's.

tools.name: kb_upsert
tools.description: Create or update one entity and its relationships. Use it for modeling, updates and every write kb_record does not take (a newly stated rule is one kb_record call). dryRun:true validates without writing. Model prose with kb_model before hand-writing strict property or predicate facts. An update keeps what it leaves out: send the changed fields (with title and status) and only the links to add. Relationship endpoints must already exist. A requirement that contradicts a current one on the same subject is rejected; to replace it, add a `supersedes` link from the new requirement and upsert the old one with status closed. For a requirement send the statement as `document.body` and the reason as `why` (never invent one: write 'Reason not stated'); give other entities a prose body. A requirement write returns its open kb_check steps as nextActions. Side effects: writes KB; dryRun:true writes nothing.

type.description: Entity type to create/update. Allowed: req, scenario, test, adr, flag, event, symbol, fact. Example: 'req'.

id.description: Unique entity ID named by the behavior it governs (<TYPE>-<area>-<behavior>); an existing ID updates the entity.

title.description: Required short title. Example: 'Protect account settings endpoint'.

status.description: Required lifecycle state; allowed values depend on the entity type. Examples: 'open', 'passing', 'accepted'.

kind.description: Who authored the entity: human, agent, migration (backfilled by kibi migrate) or import.

ref.description: Source reference for the authored content: URL, document path, ticket, commit or conversation id.

approved_by.description: The person who reviewed and approved this entity's content, not the approved_by of an exception requirement.

recorded_at.description: ISO-8601 time the provenance was recorded.

origin.description: Optional provenance: kind (human, agent, migration, import) and authority (ref, approved_by, recorded_at).

semantic_text.description: Requirement-only authored prose used for semantic inventory hashes and UTF-8 spans.

approved_by.description: Requirement-only: the human who approved this exception requirement.

approval_ref.description: Requirement-only. Optional reference to the exception's approval decision record.

firmness.description: req/adr only: firm (a human's rule, needs origin.ref), default or exploratory. Absent = default if an agent wrote it.

required_evidence.description: Requirement-only: weakest evidence level it accepts. Absent = tested if firm, else unverified.

rationale.description: Requirement-only: why it exists, in the stater's words; send it in the same write when they gave one, never invent one.

sourceFile.description: Optional code source file for symbol entities. Example: 'src/auth/login.ts'.

symbol_role.description: Optional role classification for symbol entities. Example: 'behavioral'.

properties.description: Entity fields; must include title and status. Fact, symbol, test and proof fields: kibi-usage resource operation-fields.

type.description: Relationship type, e.g. implements (symbol->req), verified_by (req/scenario->test), executable_for (symbol->test).

relationships.description: Optional relationship rows to create in the same call; asserts edges in the KB.

dryRun.description: Validate and preview without writing the KB or workspace; use it as the preflight before the real write.

type.description: Relationship type, e.g. implements (symbol->req), verified_by (req/scenario->test), executable_for (symbol->test).

relationships.description: Optional relationship rows to create in the same call; asserts edges in the KB.

plannedFacts.description: dryRun only: fact payloads (e.g. kb_model applyPlan entries) staged before this one, so their links resolve.

document.description: Optional source document write; omit body on update to keep it. New requirements take statement, Context, Source.

implementedBy.description: req only: declarations that implement it, each {sourceFile, symbol, coveredBy?}; linked by implements (and covered_by).

why.description: req only: why it exists, in the asker's words.

workspaceRoot.description: Optional absolute path of the workspace this call is about, such as your git worktree, when it is not the server's.

tools.name: kb_record
tools.description: Record a rule as it is stated: statement, why, saidBy, quote, code and an optional test. Kibi writes it as one kb_upsert payload and returns the commit gate's verdict (commitAllowed, findings with blocks) and the steps left as nextActions. dryRun:true returns the payload and writes nothing. Facts, links, updates and other modeling: kb_upsert.

statement.description: The rule as one testable must sentence.

why.description: Why it exists, in their words; 'Reason not stated' if none given.

quote.description: Their words, recorded as origin.ref; a firm rule needs one.

code.description: Declarations that implement it, each {file, symbol}.

test.description: An existing TEST id that checks it.

dryRun.description: Return the kb_upsert payload; write nothing.

workspaceRoot.description: Optional absolute path of the workspace this call is about, such as your git worktree, when it is not the server's.

tools.name: kb_delete
tools.description: Delete entities by ID, or exact relationship triples. Use only for intentional removals after dependency checks. Do not use as a bulk cleanup shortcut. An entity authored in a Markdown or YAML source is not deleted directly: the call writes nothing and returns outcome plan_returned with a hash-bound deletionPlan and a nextActions entry holding the exact kb_apply_plan input ({plan, approvedPlanHash}); apply that unmodified, or repeat this call with approvedPlanHash = deletionPlan.planHash to apply the freshly computed plan in one step (a stale or different hash fails with DELETE_PLAN_HASH_MISMATCH and writes nothing). Authored requirements are never deleted: outcome supersession_required points to kb_upsert with a supersedes relationship. dryRun:true previews any delete and writes nothing. Side effects: mutates and saves KB and authored sources; skips entities with dependents; dryRun and plan_returned write nothing.

ids.description: Entity IDs to delete after dependency checks.

relationships.description: Exact relationship triples to retract, including legacy shard records.

approvedPlanHash.description: With ids only: the deletionPlan.planHash a prior call returned; applied only while the hash still matches.

dryRun.description: Preview without writing: returns what a commit would delete and write.

workspaceRoot.description: Optional absolute path of the workspace this call is about, such as your git worktree, when it is not the server's.

tools.name: kb_check
tools.description: Run KB validation rules and return violations, quality diagnostics, and typed kibi.migration-plan.v2 actions. Use before or after mutations and after source edits; checks remain read-only and never infer or apply actions from prose suggestions.

rules.description: Optional rule names (an unknown one is refused with the list). Omit to run every rule plus the full-KB audit.

sourceFiles.description: Optional repo-relative source files to inspect for impact diagnostics; scopes violations to what they touch.

includeMigrationPlan.description: Return the full migrationPlan (for kb_apply_plan) even when the result would show only its summary.

includeSymbolDebt.description: Without rules or sourceFiles: list unrecorded declarations per file (symbolDebt has counts only by default).

staged.description: When true, inspect staged source changes for impact diagnostics, as kibi check --staged does.

changed.description: When true, give the commit gate's verdict on every current change (commitAllowed, findings with blocks).

includeWorkingTreeDiff.description: When true, inspect unstaged working-tree diffs for impact diagnostics; pair with sourceFiles to scope.

includeImpactDiagnostics.description: When true, include changed-file impact diagnostics (granularity, ownership, statements to verify) in the output.

maxDiagnostics.description: Optional maximum number of impact diagnostics to return. Graph validation violations are not capped by this value.

workspaceRoot.description: Optional absolute path of the workspace this call is about, such as your git worktree, when it is not the server's.

async.description: When true, run as a background job and return a kibi.job.v1 receipt to poll with kb_job_status.

tools.name: kb_review_firm_edit
tools.description: Record your verdict on a change to code that implements a current firm requirement: keeps (the code still does what it says) or changes. kibi check --staged blocks such a change until each edited symbol has a current keeps receipt. A receipt is your judgment, not the person's approval. staged:true reviews the code and requirement in the Git index, as the commit gate reads them. Side effects: writes .kb/firm-edit-reviews/ files; dryRun:true writes nothing.

workspaceRoot.description: Optional absolute path of the workspace this call is about, such as your git worktree, when it is not the server's.

tools.name: kb_prepare_impact_review
tools.description: Prepare complete content-bound impact-review authoring inputs from the current staged snapshot or explicitly selected immutable Git commits. Use it when kb_check reports that changed files need an impact review; it does not plan KB changes. Returns strict reviewer schemas and an unauthored template; it does not decide, approve, sign, stage, or prove the review.

scope.description: {"kind":"staged"} for the staged snapshot, or {"kind":"diff","baseCommit","headCommit"} with full hashes.

workspaceRoot.description: Optional absolute path of the workspace this call is about, such as your git worktree, when it is not the server's.

tools.name: kb_plan_bootstrap
tools.description: Generate a deterministic, snapshot-bound kibi.bootstrap-plan.v1 for repository onboarding. Use it only to onboard a repository whose KB is empty or incomplete (the kibi-bootstrap skill drives it); for a change in an onboarded project use kb_compile_intent. Read-only analysis of the repository plus any declared knowledge sources and cited intent claims returns evidence, bounded context questions, exact dependency-ordered actions, a canonical plan hash, and no mutation side effects.

includeGenericMarkdown.description: Whether to include generic markdown content as candidate facts. Default: true, or false with declared intentClaims.

minConfidence.description: Minimum confidence threshold for candidates. Clamped to [0.60, 0.95]. Default: 0.80.

maxCandidates.description: Budget for candidates Kibi discovers itself; declared intentClaims are never capped. Clamped to [1, 200]. Default: 50.

entityTypes.description: Optional filter to limit candidate generation to specific entity types.

projectSummary.description: Optional short summary of the project or bootstrap goal.

sourceOfTruthPaths.description: Optional repo-relative paths that should be treated as declared sources of truth.

sourceOfTruthNotes.description: Optional notes about how to interpret the declared sources of truth.

priorityRoots.description: Optional repo roots the bootstrap flow should prioritize when authoring entities.

verificationAnchors.description: Optional verification commands, documents, or checkpoints to reference in the output.

id.description: Stable kebab-case handle that intentClaims cite, for example jira-payments.

locator.description: Where the source lives: a URL, project key, space name, or repo-relative path.

authority.description: The human's call: authoritative, supporting, or stale (cited, never a candidate).

connector.description: Optional name of the MCP server or tool the agent used to read the source.

component.description: Optional component the source's claims are about; the first segment of each generated subject_key.

knowledgeSources.description: Knowledge sources outside the code the human confirmed (trackers, wikis, specs); the agent cites them from intentClaims.

statement.description: One normative statement in the source's meaning, for example 'Refunds must not exceed the original charge.'

sourceId.description: The id of a declared knowledge source.

reference.description: Exact citation inside the source: a ticket key, page URL, or section anchor.

excerpt.description: Verbatim passage the claim came from; required for intent and observation claims, kept in the entity's Source section.

component.description: Optional component the claim is about; generated subject keys take the shape component.aspect.

rationale.description: Optional reason the requirement exists, as the source or the human states it. Never invent one.

kind.description: intent (may become a req), observation (how things are today) or open_question. Default: intent.

intentClaims.description: Statements harvested from knowledgeSources, each citing its source and excerpt; intent claims may become requirements.

note.description: What disagrees, in one sentence, without resolving it.

conflicts.description: Contradictions between declared intentClaims left for the human; each becomes a fact tagged review:conflict.

bootstrapContext.description: Optional declared bootstrap context supplied by the agent to ground the read-only synthesis output.

workspaceRoot.description: Optional absolute path of the workspace this call is about, such as your git worktree, when it is not the server's.

tools.name: kb_compile_intent
tools.description: Compile complete change intent into a deterministic, snapshot-bound read-only plan. Use it before editing code for a change request that may touch several requirements; use kb_model for one requirement's prose and kb_plan_bootstrap for first-time onboarding. Reuses intent-aware discovery and semantic modeling, accounts for every proposition, reports contradiction witnesses, proposes traceability links, and emits dependency-ordered kb_upsert-style steps only for resolved typed claims. contradictionAnalysis.outcome is no_conflict only when the check could decide: an unmodeled proposition or a related current requirement without logic leaves it unresolved with reasons and reviewCandidates to compare and judge through conflictReviews. No mutation side effects.

intent.description: Complete post-change normative intent. Send the desired behavior, not a patch fragment.

mode.description: Create a new requirement or update an existing one.

context.description: Why the requirement exists and who asked; required for create. Write 'Reason not stated' rather than invent one.

sourceExcerpt.description: Optional verbatim text the intent came from, quoted in the Source section; requires context.

sourceReference.description: Optional locator of the source text (ticket id, URL, path) for the Source section; requires context.

requirementId.description: Optional exact requirement ID. Required for an update when automatic selection is below the confidence and margin gates.

title.description: Optional requirement title; existing title is preserved for updates when omitted.

clauses.description: Optional atomic clause decomposition; each clause must be a verbatim fragment of intent.

semanticFacets.description: Host-agent facets forwarded to deterministic intent-v1 discovery.

sourceLocations.description: Workspace-relative source coordinates used for discovery and before-hash binding.

interpretations.description: Optional host-supplied typed kibi.logic.v1 interpretations; Kibi validates them before including rule steps.

scenarioDrafts.description: Optional scenario drafts. Each is linked requirement -> scenario with specified_by.

scenarioIds.description: Stable scenario draft IDs verified by this test. Required when multiple scenario drafts are supplied.

testDrafts.description: Optional test drafts. Tests are attached to scenarios with verified_by; direct req -> test proof links are not emitted.

proposalDecisions.description: Explicit decisions for deterministic traceability proposals. Pending proposals never enter steps.

conflictReviews.description: Your verdict on each reviewCandidates entry of a previous compile; a conflict verdict blocks the plan.

workspaceRoot.description: Optional absolute path of the workspace this call is about, such as your git worktree, when it is not the server's.

tools.name: kb_apply_plan
tools.description: Apply an explicitly approved kibi.bootstrap-plan.v1, kibi.compile-plan.v1, kibi.migration-plan.v2, or entity-deletion plan after revalidating its canonical hash and live snapshots. Compile plans apply all-or-nothing: a durable journal records every source write and store mutation before the first write, all steps commit in one store transaction, and an interrupted application is completed or rolled back by the next mutating call. Bootstrap actions are dependency-ordered, sequential, source-first, and recoverable from a typed journal.

approvedPlanHash.description: Exact SHA-256 planHash returned by kb_plan_bootstrap, kb_compile_intent, or another approved plan after human review.

plan.description: The complete bootstrap, compile, migration or hash-bound entity-deletion plan object to apply.

approvedActionIds.description: Required for migration-plan.v2: the exact action IDs approved for this application.

recoveryJournalId.description: Recovery journal id from a committed_with_repairs result or PLAN_APPLY_RECOVERY_REQUIRED error, to resume.

async.description: MCP only: when true, run as a background job and return a kibi.job.v1 receipt to poll with kb_job_status.

workspaceRoot.description: Optional absolute path of the workspace this call is about, such as your git worktree, when it is not the server's.

tools.name: kb_ingest_proof
tools.description: Ingest a producer-emitted kibi.proof-run.v1 artifact and evaluate it against each selected test's kibi.proof-contract.v1 proof obligations. Revalidates the live workspace snapshot, integration command binding, run-level outcome, attempt history, success policy, and append-only proof-receipt history before deriving and appending idempotent kibi.proof-receipt.v1 receipts. Producers report what happened; Kibi evaluates proof. Prefer `kibi prove` so the configured producer runs automatically; direct ingestion is an integration path for custom producers and agents.

snapshot.description: Workspace snapshot captured immediately before the run.

target.description: Ecosystem-neutral execution target (browser, runtime, database, device, deployment, or default).

items.description: One observed proof result; attempts report facts only.

certificates.description: kibi.code-certificate.v1 objects for certificate-kind contracts, one per test; Kibi re-checks each.

artifact.description: Producer-emitted kibi.proof-run.v1 artifact, from kibi prove or a direct call; Kibi evaluates the obligations.

testIds.description: Existing test entities with proof_contract.v1. Omit to evaluate every test contracted to the artifact's integration.

workspaceRoot.description: Optional absolute path of the workspace this call is about, such as your git worktree, when it is not the server's.

instructions:
Kibi records this repository's requirements and decisions with their reasons.
- Before changing behaviour, kb_search for the recorded intent and kb_query the requirement that governs it.
- When the person states a rule, record it with their reason (kb_record); a decision goes through kb_upsert.
- Before finishing, stage the change with its .kb files and run the commit check, `kibi check --staged`.
A request that would make a recorded requirement or decision false (narrowing it or adding an exception counts; touching its code does not) is a question, not a task: name the rule and ask.
kb_search answers a question with the governing requirements, facts, ADRs and tests; kb_query looks up an exact id or sourceFile; kb_record records a stated rule; kb_upsert writes and models; kb_check validates; kb_status reports freshness.
Workflow guidance: kb_skills with action load and id kibi-usage. For first-time repository setup, use the kibi-bootstrap prompt.

[KIBI-MCP] Kibi collects anonymous usage statistics (operation names, durations, error categories and versions) to improve Kibi.
It never sends code, file paths, queries, KB content or repository names.
Turn it off with `kibi telemetry disable` or KIBI_TELEMETRY=0. Details: https://looted.github.io/kibi/guide/telemetry.html
